name: Dorn method

card.summary: The Dorn method is a gentle manual therapy aimed at realigning the spine and joints, used by people hoping that better alignment improves posture and how they carry themselves.
card.note: A manual alternative therapy; no clinical studies are cited on its Wikipedia page.

quick.overview:
The Dorn method is a manual, holistic alternative therapy meant to correct misalignments in the spinal column and other joints. Practitioners feel along the spine and apply gentle pressure while the client makes guided movements.

For looks, the connection people draw runs through posture: a better-aligned spine and pelvis is said to give a more upright stance, which changes how tall and balanced someone appears. Enthusiasts online also mention it for back and sacrum discomfort that interferes with training.
quick.how: A practitioner checks the spine by touch. Where an area seems unbalanced, they apply light thumb or hand pressure against the spinous processes while the client swings a leg or arm or makes other guided movements. Clients are advised to stop if they feel pain. Self-help sacrum exercise videos circulate on video platforms.
quick.risks: Manual therapies applied to the spine carry the general caution that pain or worsening symptoms should be reported to a clinician. Wikipedia's article cites no clinical studies of the method.

lead: The Dorn method is described on Wikipedia as a manual, holistic alternative therapy used to correct misalignments in the spinal column and other joints [1]. In a session the practitioner palpates the spine; if a region seems unbalanced, they press gently with thumb or hand against the spinous processes while the client moves a limb in guided ways, a principle the article likens to counter pressure [1].

People interested in appearance approach it through posture and structure: if the spine, pelvis and legs are aligned, proponents say, someone stands more upright and carries themselves better, and back or sacrum discomfort that limits exercise may ease. A poster in a T Nation lower-back-pain thread recommended Dorn method sacrum self-help exercise videos for this purpose [2].
The Wikipedia article is a stub whose only source is a 2009 lifestyle magazine feature and cites no scientific studies [1].

chain: Gentle guided pressure on spine and joints
Perceived better alignment of spine, pelvis and legs
angle.text: Proponents use it for alignment and back comfort. The appearance payoff they describe is better posture and easier training, rather than any change in bone structure.

infobox: Gentle pressure with guided limb movement [1]

paras: According to Wikipedia, the practitioner palpates the spine and, where something seems unbalanced, applies gentle pressure with the thumb or hand to the spinous processes while the client performs movements such as swinging an arm or leg. The article describes the idea as similar to counter pressure in mechanics, and clients are told to stop if it hurts [1].

The method appears in strength-training forums as something people try for lower-back or sacrum problems, for instance via sacrum self-help exercise videos recommended in a 2010 T Nation thread [2]. In posture-focused discussion it is grouped with other alignment approaches.
